causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Calm conditions meant wind generation across the three regions was very low. Of the 6,510 MW of installed semi scheduled wind capacity, only between 320 MW and 430 MW of electricity was generated by wind during the high priced intervals.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Across the three regions almost 4,000 MW of baseload generation was unavailable. Two thirds of this capacity was undergoing planned maintenance, as expected during the lower demand periods of spring and autumn.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Across the three regions almost 4,000 MW of baseload generation was unavailable. One third was unplanned due to various technical plant issues.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: By 6 pm on both evenings there was no solar generation available in NSW and Victoria, meaning grid supply was reduced and grid demand increased as consumers switched from consuming some electricity from their rooftop PV to the grid instead.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand was high during the evening peak, driven by cooler weather increasing heating requirements.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Upgrades on the Queensland-NSW Interconnector (QNI) meant flow from Queensland into NSW was around 700 MW, while its nominal limit is over 1,000 MW.

interconnectors_named.name: Queensland-NSW Interconnector (QNI)
interconnectors_named.quote: Upgrades on the Queensland-NSW Interconnector (QNI) meant flow from Queensland into NSW was around 700 MW, while its nominal limit is over 1,000 MW.
